title: Role hierarchy construction determines the public decision
summary: The legacy and fluent graphs propagate A to B and B to C and D under either prefix. A real authority manager decides from the selected authorities.

change.description: The legacy and fluent graphs propagate A to B and B to C and D under either prefix. A real authority manager decides from the selected authorities.

notes: The pre-feature artifact supplies the legacy API only. The client links its optional builder path against landed code and executes it only where the original runtime provides it. The historical core uses the setup graph with released 6.2.0 crypto. The release graph uses Security 6.3.0 and Framework 6.1.7.

Each prefix granted 14 of the 16 authority subsets. The distinct before, feature, landed and release JARs were loaded on the JVM. The 64-history combined caller made 56 third edits and preserved the field error even on all eight declined writes.

Gating all three edits on the release JVM covered 98,304 histories across both bean layouts, both prefixes, every edit order and all authority subsets at each step. The manager granted 258,048 of 294,912 attempts. All 10,752 declines after an earlier invalid edit retained its field error and rejected value. Cases 1057 and 82977 distinguish a wrong first submission through the final bean and the final ledger respectively.

First startup recheck (20261123-011836). Both original legacy hierarchies established the exact reachable names and the real manager decision for all 32 prefix/subset configurations. The fluent builder enters the real StringWriter constructor and stops at PrintWriter's bootstrap helper before emitting the hierarchy text.

Both unguarded fluent claims now reach the first PrintWriter line terminator. On all 32 selectors a strict native proof checks both original fluent claims whenever the JVM uses LF or CRLF. The checker executes the actual ordered map callback and writes into the original StringBuffer. LF and CRLF admit the same original public outcomes. On a literal pipe only 10 of 32 name sets and 20 of 32 decisions agree with the intended graph.

The original default Linux and explicit CRLF launches each discharge the native fluent guard for all 32 configurations, even after changing the live line.separator property. A pipe leaves the guard inactive. The two unrestricted fluent obligations still first need the startup separator.
